image_alt: A diagram showing the core principle of how the CurvePotGCN model predicts protein-protein interactions. In the center are the surfaces of two opposing protein molecules, differing in shape and color. The protein on the left has a concave surface with blue areas, representing positive electrostatic potential; the protein on the right has a convex surface with red areas, representing negative electrostatic potential. This complementary "lock-and-key" shape and "opposites-attract" charge visually explains the physical basis for how the two proteins can bind. The image illustrates how the model uses these two fundamental features—surface curvature and electrostatic potential—to determine if an interaction exists, highlighting the method's simple and effective approach.
